hook_patterns: The 'Self-Diagnosis' Hook: Framing a psychological concept as a trait the viewer secretly possesses.
The 'Failing Perception' Hook: Challenging the viewer's brain to process a visual or cognitive paradox in real-time.
The 'Hidden Rules' Hook: Revealing secret subconscious influences behind everyday objects, colors, or behaviors.
todays_angle: Translate foundational public-domain psychological concepts (like William James or Sigmund Freud) into practical self-awareness checks about subconscious behavior.

ideas.title: 3 Signs Your Subconscious is Buried in Stress (According to 1910 Psychology)
ideas.hook: Show a classic vintage diagram of the brain while asking: 'Are you doing these 3 things without realizing it?'
ideas.concept: Uses concepts from early psychoanalysis (e.g., Freud's repression mechanisms) to explain modern physical nervous ticks, creating an authoritative listicle format.

ideas.title: The 100-Year-Old Color Trick That Manipulates Your Mood
ideas.hook: Display a striking dual-color archival illustration: 'Your brain reacts to this tint before you even notice it.'
ideas.concept: Draws from early 20th-century perception literature (Gestalt psychology) to explain how specific visual inputs alter emotional states.

ideas.title: Why Introverts Process Noise Differently (1921 Carl Jung Theory)
ideas.hook: Voiceover over a classic black-and-white portrait: 'If crowded rooms exhaust you instantly, your brain does this.'
ideas.concept: Adapts Carl Jung's original definitions of Psychological Types into an empowering, relatable breakdown of introverted cognitive processing.

avoid: Generic motivational quote compilations with low-effort text overlays and generic stock footage.
Hyper-sensationalized 'Dark Psychology' clickbait that lacks actual historical or scientific substance.
